source_method: Effective PDF 2.0 plus EC3; physical page is printed page + 15. The alternate-image algorithm is amended by Issue #79 markup, so extracted body text alone is insufficient.

features.source_location: printed 255, physical 270; heading 'Image parameters'. The paragraph states four interrelated image parameters: format, data, user-space correspondence, and sample-to-colour mapping.
features.assessment: The standalone image_coordinates_audit fixture supplies a valid 3x2 DeviceRGB image with explicit width, height, 8-bit samples, stream data, placement matrix, and literal six-color expectations. It demonstrates all four parameter roles in one valid XObject; it is not an exhaustive assertion for every image format or colour family. The broader format and mapping families belong to the separately reviewed image decoding shards.
features.verdict: supported for the sampled valid XObject; clause-wide assertion inventory not repeated here
residuals: This focused render fixture does not enumerate all image codecs, component counts, or colour-space families.

features.source_location: printed 255-256, physical 270-271; heading 'Sample representation'. Specifies high-order-bit-first packing, row byte alignment, unsigned sample values, and component interleaving; physical 271 contains the component-interleaving and sample-grid prose.
features.assessment: The ledger's named packing tests target byte-row restart, bit order and 16-bit byte order; the coordinate audit's six independently literal RGB samples additionally asserts row-major component/sample interpretation through the public render path. The coordinate fixture uses 8-bit components, so it is not evidence for the other bit depths; those are separately asserted in bit_depths.rs.
features.verdict: sampled assertions align with the cited representation features
residuals: This shard did not re-audit every bit-depth, inline-image, or codec-specific representation path.

features.source_location: printed 256-257, physical 271-272; heading 'Image coordinate system'. The image-space origin is upper-left, sample cells are row-major, and [1/w 0 0 -1/h 0 1] maps source coordinates into the unit square; printed 257 carries the matrix and Figure 49.
features.assessment: Strong discriminating public-render coverage: a 3x2 grid with six distinct literal colours is placed into a 60x60 square, then under reflection and skew. Assertions cover row orientation, aspect-ratio independence, both transform columns and outside-image white controls. The exact-xref helper asserts Document::was_recovered() is false and interpretation completeness; expected pixels derive directly from the encoded sample bytes and stated matrices.
features.verdict: strong focused coverage of the source-to-user coordinate mapping
residuals: CPU raster is the literal pixel oracle; the separate existing render-cpu image_placement suite covers ordinary placement and the ledger separately names GPU, but this audit did not execute or re-audit every backend.

features.source_location: printed 263, physical 278; heading 'Image interpolation'. Table 87 is printed 259, physical 274: /Interpolate is optional boolean, default false. The clause states the flag is only a hint and a processor may ignore it.
features.assessment: The public-render fixture has exact xref offsets, valid 2x1 grayscale samples, normal and reflected placement, explicit false versus absent default controls, stable source-interior samples and seam controls. It asserts the current CPU bilinear outcome for true; the test comment explicitly identifies this as local policy. Exact bilinear values are not a normative conformance oracle because the source permits ignoring the hint and does not prescribe a filter kernel. The dispatch parser uses only boolean true as enabled and otherwise defaults false.
features.verdict: flag plumbing/default supported; filter-kernel assertion is implementation policy, not a normative requirement
residuals: No normative requirement to produce bilinear/mixed pixels, nor to honor true, is inferred. Backend-specific filtering equivalence was not asserted.

features.source_location: printed 264-265, physical 279-280; Table 89 printed 264/physical 279. Effective Issue #79 EC3 markups: physical 279 replaces terminal-hidden wording and printing selection; physical 280 replaces ordinary alternate selection and adds step (e). Footer confirms printed pages 264-265.
features.primary_markup_evidence: pikepdf inspection of Issue #79 annotations: physical 279 replacement caret says hidden base content -> nothing; another says printed + any DefaultForPrinting true -> that alternate printed. Physical 280 replacement caret says choose first alternate with visible /OC, skip entries lacking /OC, and do not inspect selected /Image stream's own /OC; a text annotation adds step (e): if c/d identify none, render base. Strikeout annotation rectangles on both pages mark superseded text; raw pdftotext includes that struck text.
features.assessment: Existing synthetic valid PDF fixtures assert source-derived black/white pixel identities and named controls for each relevant branch: hidden/visible base, first visible alternate versus later candidate, no-/OC alternate skipped, no selected alternate falls back to base, print-only DefaultForPrinting, base /OC prevents alternate selection, and selected alternate's image-stream /OC is not rechecked. These are end-to-end interpretation/raster tests. The code path is split correctly between base visibility in draw_xobject and c/d selection in alternate_image. Table 89 allows at most one print-designated entry; malformed multiple designations are not elevated into a new normative case.
features.verdict: effective amended algorithm is implemented and meaningfully asserted for sampled paths
residuals: No corpus PDF in the recorded census exercises /Alternates; evidence is synthetic. This shard did not exhaust Table 89 malformed-entry handling or re-audit optional-content expression semantics.
